issue.title: `gh pr list` with flags fails JSON parsing
issue.author: yrahul3910

summary.headline: Filtered `gh pr list` fails with a JSON error because go-gh's HTTP cache served an entry corrupted by a non-atomic write
summary.tldr: With a filter flag, `gh pr list` runs a cached `SearchType_enumValues` feature-detection query. go-gh's `fileStorage.store` (pkg/api/cache.go) rewrote cache files in place, so parallel gh processes could corrupt an entry, and `fileStorage.read` served it unchecked until shurcooL-graphql's JSON decoder failed. go-gh #263 made writes atomic (temp file + rename) and shipped in gh v2.101.0 via cli/cli #14461; entries corrupted before that still need `gh config clear-cache` (go-gh #300 is open).

flow.title: What happens when you run gh pr list --author "@me"

steps.title: pr list wraps its HTTP client in a 24-hour cache
steps.detail: The reporter ran `gh pr list --author "@me"`. `listRun` builds the feature detector on `api.NewCachedHTTPClient(httpClient, time.Hour*24)`, which only adds an `X-GH-CACHE-TTL: 24h0m0s` header to each request (api/http_client.go#L135-L151). The header is visible on the failing request in the reporter's `GH_DEBUG=api` log.

steps.title: Filter flags switch pr list to the search path
steps.detail: `--author`, `--search`, `--label`, `--assignee` and `--draft` make `shouldUseSearch` true, so `searchPullRequests` runs and first calls `detector.SearchFeatures()` (http.go#L37-L40). Plain `gh pr list` takes the `NewLister` branch and never touches the cached detector, which is why it kept working.

steps.title: Detector asks the API for the SearchType enum values
steps.detail: `SearchFeatures` sends the `SearchType_enumValues` introspection query through the cached client via `api.Client.Query` (api/client.go#L134-L142), which hands off to go-gh's GraphQL client. Because it is a POST to `/graphql`, go-gh treats it as cacheable.

steps.title: On a cache miss the response is fetched, then stored
steps.detail: `RoundTrip` hashes method, URL, Accept, Authorization and body into a key (`cacheKey`, L55-L73). If no fresh file exists it calls the network and then `crt.fs.store(key, res)`, ignoring any store error. Any gh process that runs the same query against the same host with the same token computes the same key and the same file path.

steps.title: Cache entry rewritten in place with no temp file
steps.detail:
`store` opens the final cache file with `O_TRUNC` and serialises the response straight into it with `res.Write(f)`. The only guard is `fs.mu`, a `sync.RWMutex` created per round tripper (L75-L81), so it serialises writers inside one process but not across gh processes. Two processes writing the same entry, or a process killed mid-write, can leave a file that is neither response.

The go-gh issue (#252) describes exactly this; the maintainer linked this report to it. That this reporter's file was corrupted by a concurrent write rather than an interrupted one is likely, not shown: the reporter did not say whether gh was running in parallel.

fix.label: go-gh PR #263
fix.detail: Write to `os.CreateTemp(dir, ".gh-cache-*")`, close it, then rename it over the entry (`renameCacheFile`), so readers only ever see a complete file. Released in go-gh v2.16.1.

refs.label: go-gh #252: API cache is not write-atomic

steps.title: Another gh process writes the same entry at the same time
steps.detail: A second gh invocation (for example several agents or scripts running gh in parallel) misses the cache for the same key and runs the same `store` code against the same path. Its in-process mutex does not exclude the first process, so both `res.Write(f)` calls write into one file. Likely, per go-gh #252 and the maintainer's comment that gh is now often run as many parallel instances.

steps.title: Cache file holds a corrupted JSON body
steps.detail: The entry lives under gh's cache dir (`config.CacheDir()`, set in go-gh `NewHTTPClient`, http_client.go#L79-L86) at `<key[0:2]>/<key[2:4]>/<rest>`. In the reporter's log the stored body starts `{"{"data":{"SearchType"...`: HTTP framing still parses, but the JSON has an extra `{"` in front. The entry stays valid for 24 hours from its mtime.

steps.title: Later run serves the corrupt entry without checking it
steps.detail: On the reporter's run `RoundTrip` finds the file, `read` checks only its age against the TTL and parses it with `http.ReadResponse`, and `RoundTrip` returns it as the response (L106-L108). Nothing checks the body. The log confirms a cache hit: `Request took 463.708µs`, and the response `Date` (01:18:38 GMT) is about 14 hours older than the request (15:06 GMT).

steps.title: JSON decoder rejects the cached body
steps.detail: go-gh's `GraphQLClient.QueryWithContext` calls `c.client.QueryNamed` (graphql_client.go#L152-L169), which lands in shurcooL-graphql `do` (v0.0.4, the version go-gh v2.16.0 requires). The decoder reads `{`, then the string `"{"` as an object key, then finds `d` where it expects `:`, and returns `invalid character 'd' after object key` unwrapped. go-gh only rewraps `graphql.Errors`, so this error passes through as is.

steps.title: Feature detection returns the decode error unchanged
steps.detail: `api.handleResponse` only converts go-gh `HTTPError` and `GraphQLError` values, so it falls through to `return err` (api/client.go#L318-L342). `SearchFeatures` returns it, `searchPullRequests` returns it (http.go#L37-L40), and `listRun` returns it (list.go#L199-L202). No context is added on the way up.

steps.title: gh prints the bare JSON error and exits
steps.detail: `Main` gets the error from `rootCmd.ExecuteContextC` and calls `printError` (cmd.go#L195-L226), which prints it with `fmt.Fprintln(out, err)`. The user sees only `invalid character 'd' after object key`, with no hint that a cache entry is at fault. Every filtered `gh pr list` fails the same way until the entry expires or `gh config clear-cache` removes it.

nodes.title: gh pr list with filter flags fails: invalid character 'd' after object key
nodes.detail: `gh pr list --author "@me"` and `--search ...` fail; plain `gh pr list` works.

nodes.title: gh 2.100.0, GitHub Enterprise repo, requests to api.github.com
Cached SearchType_enumValues body starts with {"{"data"
nodes.detail: The GH_DEBUG=api log shows the failing response came back in 463µs with a Date header hours older than the request, and httpretty reports `body cannot be formatted: invalid character 'd' after object key`.

nodes.title: Triage bot traces the failure to cached feature detection
nodes.detail: Points at the `SearchType_enumValues` query in featuredetection and the on-disk response cache; mechanism left open.

nodes.title: gh config clear-cache makes the command work again
A one-off glitch, nothing to fix
nodes.detail: The reporter closed the issue after clearing the cache.

nodes.title: go-gh cache writes are not atomic across processes
nodes.detail: `fileStorage.store` truncates and rewrites the live cache file; its mutex is per process. Already reported as go-gh #252; the maintainer reopened this issue and linked it.

nodes.title: go-gh #263: publish HTTP cache entries without in-place writes
go-gh #300: evict cache entries that fail an integrity check
nodes.detail: Follow-up so entries corrupted before #263 heal themselves instead of needing clear-cache.

edges.note: Removing cache files removes the failure
Maintainer reopened: a known go-gh cache race
Would self-heal entries corrupted before the fix

open_questions: Whether the reporter's entry was corrupted by two parallel gh processes or by a gh process that died mid-write; the exact byte sequence that produced the leading {" was not reconstructed.
Whether users on gh v2.101.0+ still hit this from entries corrupted before upgrading (go-gh #300 is still open).
next_steps: Review and merge go-gh #300 so corrupt entries are evicted and refetched, then bump go-gh in cli/cli.
Until then, tell affected users to run `gh config clear-cache`.
